target.title: security(audit): flag control-plane exposure and plugin command surfaces
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two related gaps in `openclaw security audit` where operators could miss high-impact exposure on open chat surfaces and extension plugin command entry points.

### Gap 1: Control-plane tools on open inbound policy

When a channel uses `groupPolicy="open"` or an open DM policy, prompt injection in those conversations can drive agent tool calls. The exposure matrix already flagged elevated tools and runtime/filesystem tools, but did **not** separately flag **control-plane tools** (`cron`, `gateway`) that can reconfigure the gateway or manipulate scheduled runs.

A common example: `tools.profile="coding"` on an open WhatsApp group allows `cron` while runtime/fs may be sandboxed — the audit could report a clean runtime/fs posture while `cron` remained reachable from untrusted chat input.

### Gap 2: Extension plugin commands on chat command surfaces

The plugin trust audit warned when extensions existed without `plugins.allow`, but severity escalation depended only on native skill commands being enabled. It did not evaluate **native command** surfaces separately, name which channels expose command surfaces in the finding detail, or warn when **enabled extension plugins register commands** that may be reachable on those surfaces.

Plugin commands bypass the LLM and run before built-in commands and agent invocation.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Control-plane exposure:** `collectRiskyToolExposureContexts()` in `audit-extra.sync.ts` now probes `cron` and `gateway` alongside existing runtime/fs checks. Emits new finding `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane` (critical) when open inbound policy is present and any agent context allows control-plane tools. Sandbox mode is explicitly not a mitigation here, unlike runtime/exec tools.

**Plugin command surface audit:** `collectPluginsTrustFindings()` in `audit-plugins-trust.ts` adds `collectConfiguredCommandSurfaces()` which resolves per-channel native commands and native skill commands. Changes:

| checkId | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` | warn; critical only when native skill commands enabled | critical when native commands **or** skill commands enabled; detail names affected channels |
| `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` | did not exist | warn when enabled extensions register commands and native commands are configured |

**Docs:** Updated `docs/gateway/security/audit-checks.md` to use the correct `plugins.allow` config key (was `plugins.allowlist`) in the `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` row.

## User Impact

* Operators running `openclaw security audit` get clearer, actionable findings when open chats can reach gateway/cron control or extension plugin commands.
* `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` may now report `critical` on setups that previously showed `warn` when native commands (not just native skills) are active without `plugins.allow`.
* No runtime behavior change: gateway, tool policy, plugin loading, and command dispatch are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Focused tests (2 files, 6 tests):**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    --config test/vitest/vitest.config.ts \
    src/security/audit-plugins-trust.test.ts \
    src/security/audit-trust-model.test.ts \
    --reporter=verbose

 ✓ security audit install metadata findings > evaluates install metadata findings                           270ms
 ✓ security audit install metadata findings > evaluates phantom allowlist findings                           10ms
 ✓ security audit install metadata findings > ignores install backup and debris dirs                          7ms
 ✓ security audit install metadata findings > does not report bundled provider plugins as phantom entries     3ms
 ✓ security audit extension tool reachability findings > evaluates extension tool reachability findings      23ms
 ✓ security audit trust model findings > evaluates trust-model exposure findings                              9ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
   Duration  1.99s
```

**Environment:** macOS (Darwin), Node.js v22.22.0

**Test matrix coverage:**

| Scenario | Expected finding | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| Open WhatsApp group + `tools.profile="coding"` | `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane` | critical |
| Same + `agents.defaults.sandbox.mode="all"` | No `open_groups_with_runtime_or_fs`; no `open_groups_with_control_plane` when automation denied | — |
| Open group + `deny: ["group:automation"]` | No `open_groups_with_control_plane` | — |
| Discord allowlist + multi-user heuristic + runtime/automation denied | `security.trust_model.multi_user_heuristic` detail includes "No exposed control-plane contexts detected." | warn |
| Extensions present, no `plugins.allow`, no configured channels | `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` | warn |
| Extensions + configured Discord (native commands auto-enabled) + no `plugins.allow` | `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` with "Native commands are enabled" in detail | **critical** |
| `plugins.allow=["some-plugin"]` + Discord + plugin registers commands | `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` | warn |
| Same + `commands.native=false` | No `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` | — |

**What was not tested:** Full `openclaw security audit --deep` against a live gateway. Regression tests import production collectors (`collectExposureMatrixFindings`, `collectPluginsTrustFindings`) directly and exercise all table-driven cases above.

## Non-goals and boundaries

* Does not change tool allow/deny enforcement at runtime.
* Does not add new config keys or env vars.
* `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` is heuristic: reports registry-registered commands on enabled extensions when native command surfaces are configured; does not live-probe channel APIs.

## AI-assisted disclosure

* AI-assisted (Cursor agent)
* Human-directed scope and review of audit logic
